text:
jordan: quick brain-dump — proposal to build an auth-proxy-shim that rewrites inbound org-key headers into ephemeral project-scoped access tokens. aim: avoid immediate rekey but move customers to project-first RBAC. thoughts?

meera: sounds feasible. key concerns: 1) preserving audit lineage, 2) revocation semantics, 3) UX for long-running jobs.

dan: agree w/ meera. For audit we should include both `x-origin-key-id` and `x-delegation-id` on downstream requests, and ensure logs redact full key id but keep suffix.

tia: revocation idea: introduce an incrementing key-version claim `kv.ver` in delegated tokens. If customer rotates or revokes, bump version in a signed mapping file and publish a revocation event. shim keeps small in-memory version map to reject older `kv.ver`.

jordan: nice. TTL proposal: short `access_token` TTL=600s (10m), optional `refresh_token` TTL=3600s (1h) for server-side background workers that explicitly opt-in during migration. streaming clients should use refresh flow not long-lived org keys.

meera: 10m is reasonable. For background jobs, require migration CLI `rw-auth convert --org-key k_XXX --target service-id:srv-YYY` which creates a service principal and rotates credentials. keep a migration grace window (12 months).

dan: mapping storage: prefer customer-managed signed JSON/YAML in S3 + signature envelope (ed25519 sig). shim validates signature before applying mapping. also keep a cached copy in the shim with TTL and a manual `force-reload` endpoint.

tia: on stateless vs stateful mapping: hybrid approach seems best — mapping rules signed (stateless) but maintain a stateful revocation/allowlist cache for emergency take-downs. revocation events via pub/sub to all shim instances.

jordan: API sketch: `POST /v1/delegate` body `{ "x_org_key": "k_XXX", "scope": "project:alpha:reader" }` -> response `{ "access_token":"t_AAA","expires_in":600,"refresh_token":"r_BBB" }`. include response header `x-delegation-id`.

meera: telemetry: emit `auth.proxy.delegate{outcome,origin_key_type,customer_size}` and `auth.proxy.revocation{hit|miss}`. Also log `delegation_id` and masked `origin_key` in audit.

deploy-bot: deploy-check: require canary in us-west and eu-west, per-instance RPS limit 150, global burst limiter 2k rps, circuit-breaker -> noop rewrite (legacy behavior).

dan: fallback semantics: if shim is unhealthy and we fall back to legacy, annotate `x-auth-fallback:legacy` header and write to `auth.fallbacks` stream. teams must be aware fallback may expand token semantics.

tia: security review notes: threat scenarios—privilege escalation via incorrect mappings, replay of delegated tokens, signing key compromise. mitigations: short TTLs, signed mappings, HSM for signing keys, TLS pinning between shim and KMS.

jordan: migration plan:
1) internal-only shim behind feature flag, simulation mode (vcalls allowed but not issued)
2) telemetry-only mode that issues tokens but with `x-simulated:true` in logs and no external release
3) invite beta customers with per-customer FF and hard mint quotas
4) gradual opt-in + 12mo deprecation for org-keys

meera: add SDK helpers: `rw-sdk auth.delegate()` and `rw-cli rw-auth convert` with dry-run option. docs + runbook for debugging (how to inspect `delegation_id`).

dan: cross-project usage: we should support multi-project scope in mapping grammar: e.g. `projects: [{id:alpha,roles:[reader]},{id:beta,roles:[writer]}]` and shim can mint per-project tokens or a batch token bundle. prefer per-project tokens to minimize blast radius.

tia: we should support an allowlist `allowed_origins` in mapping to prevent keys being used from unexpected IPs / regions. also require admin attestation field in mapping metadata.

jordan: operational bits: provide `POST /v1/adapter/reload` and `GET /v1/adapter/status` with `revocation_cache_size` and `last_sync`. propagate `trace_id` to logs.

meera: add audit-id propagation: each delegation must include `audit_id` UUID which is persisted in the cust S3 audit dump. helps reconstruct chain: origin key -> delegation -> downstream call.

deploy-bot: noted: will enforce rate-limits and create canary job. add runbook step to rollback by toggling FF and purging revocation cache.

dan: one more thing: billing tags — ensure `x-billing-tags` survive delegation mapping so chargeback remains accurate.

tia: agree. also add `auth.delegate.errors` histogram to detect mapping mismatches.

jordan: ok i'll draft RFC w/ these sections: API, mapping format, signing, TTLs, revocation pub/sub, telemetry + runbook. request reviewers: @meera (mapping + SDK), @dan (ops & billing), @tia (security), @sec (full review).

sec: i'll take the threat model and pen-test sign-off. ensure token introspection endpoint exists for ops but gated behind auth and audit.

jordan: thanks all — sync Thurs 11am to lock TTLs and the hybrid mapping model. add anything else before EOD. :thumbsup:
